html:
SMTO-LLM-0024 — The model service is limiting how many requests SMTO can send

GUID: faef6d88-9642-4fbf-b7a2-26beecf54def
Slug: provider-rate-limited
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model service declined the request because a speed or usage limit was reached. Sending the same request again right away won't lift the limit.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a few minutes, and pause other tasks or apps that use the same model account. Speed limits clear after a short time, and fewer requests at once stay under them.
  2. Check your account with the model provider for a usage limit or quota that has run out. A used-up quota doesn't clear by waiting a few minutes; it needs the provider account changed.
  3. Once the limit has cleared, on the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). The declined request did nothing, so continuing is safe and earlier finished steps are kept.

What success looks like

  • The task continues and the model replies without this error.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages your model service account; they may need to raise the limit. Don't keep selecting Resume over and over, because repeated requests can keep the limit in place.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The provider rejected the request with HTTP 429 (provider_rate_limited) because a request, usage or capacity limit applied; the response does not say which.

What this means

  • HTTP 429 means the provider declined the request because a request, usage or capacity limit applied. The response alone does not distinguish those provider limits. Repeated immediate submissions can prolong the problem.

Why this can happen

  • The provider applied a rate or usage limit; its account or service records identify which limit.

How to diagnose it

  • Check any provider retry interval and the account’s quota or concurrency limits. A depleted quota requires a different correction from a brief concurrency limit.

How to fix it

  • Honor any retry interval the provider returns, and check the account's rate, concurrency and quota limits with the provider. Reduce concurrent SMTO tasks sharing the account, then resume once the limit clears; repeated immediate submissions can prolong it.
  • Wait for the provider’s stated retry interval, if supplied, and check quota or concurrency limits with the provider operator. Preserve earlier work before a new model request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • An admitted request completes after the applicable limit is cleared.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Status classification describes this model request and grants no authority to replay earlier tools.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
